Takes are the two after-the-close reports where the story itself changed (RCAT down, ACM up) and the one rotation with its own earnings driver (payroll processors against software on a Fed about to hike). The rest of the screen is the defensive bid with no news of its own, or an earnings bet inside the week.

Same tape as the night pass (SPY -1.9%, QQQ -2.7%, third down day on the AI trade, Nvidia Tuesday after the close, Anthropic lists Thursday; futures flat at 10:40 PM CT). This screen is the part the night pass did not judge: mostly the defensive bid seen as basket spreads, and oversold or overbought names with no turn. Two takes, each with a driver of its own that does not need Nvidia to go one way: HubSpot on its founder's return and his $5M purchase, and paint makers against materials on falling oil. The rest are passed as bets on which way Nvidia breaks the tape, or as stretched names where the story that stretched them is still running.

No takes: all 17 candidates are the screen's weakest setup (stretched, no turn), each stretch is explained by an event 5 to 13 sessions old with nothing dated inside the window to turn it, and the shorts (the defensive bid) and longs (what was sold) are together one bet on the tape after Nvidia.

Flat tape waiting on Nvidia after the close (SPY -0.1%, VIX 23.0, 10-year 5.14%, WTI +1.6%). The screen is breakdowns in what has been sold for a week (quantum, Super Micro, rare earths, AGNC) and fades of the defensive bid. One take: AGNC short against long Treasuries, where the driver is the Fed and mortgage spreads, not tonight's report. The rest are passed as bets on which way Nvidia breaks the tape, or as stretches with nothing dated to turn them.

Second day of selling into Nvidia's report after the close (SPY -1.1% on its 200-day, VIX 25.9, 10-year 5.09%, WTI +0.8%); software is the day's hole (IGV -3.3%, Salesforce -9% on no news) as funds make room for Anthropic's listing. The screen is 20 breakdowns in what has been sold for weeks and 10 stretches with nothing dated to turn them. One take: BILL, where the FT says TPG is days from a take-private, a story that does not depend on tonight. The rest are passed: a short opened this afternoon in things already down 10-40% is a bet on which way Nvidia breaks the tape, and the hedged ones had no news of their own.
